privacy.ai_training_note: Fortinet's privacy policy does not explicitly address ML/AI model training on customer data or opt-out mechanisms. The policy states Fortinet may use data 'to improve services and develop new features' but does not specify whether this includes training ML models. For Processor Data (customer data Fortinet handles), companies must request choices directly through their Fortinet customer account, or contact dsar@fortinet.com.
privacy.data_region: Multiple regions with regional data hosting options. Lacework's historical policy mentioned EU data hosted in Frankfurt, APAC data in Australia. Now subject to Fortinet's data residency policies.

products.name: FortiCNAPP - Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)
products.data_scope: Scans cloud infrastructure configurations (AWS, Azure, GCP) for misconfigurations and compliance violations
products.notes: Supports compliance mapping for SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, NIST, FedRAMP

products.name: FortiCNAPP - Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP)
products.data_scope: Runtime protection for containerized workloads and Kubernetes environments
products.notes: Detects threats in running containers and orchestration platforms

products.name: FortiCNAPP - Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM)
products.data_scope: Analyzes cloud identity permissions and access across multi-cloud environments
products.notes: Continuous visibility into user roles, groups, and excessive permissions

products.name: FortiCNAPP - Cloud Detection and Response (CDR)

products.name: FortiCNAPP - Code Security (SAST/SCA/IaC)

products.notes: Shift-left security with SAST, SCA, and IaC scanning capabilities

flags: Lacework was acquired by Fortinet on August 1, 2024. The product is now branded FortiCNAPP (formerly Lacework).

Lacework's historical SOC 2 Type II (September 2018) predates the Fortinet acquisition. It is unclear whether this certification carries forward under Fortinet/FortiCNAPP or whether a new assessment was required post-acquisition.

FortiCNAPP marketing materials state the product 'supports' or 'maps to' compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS). This describes a product feature that helps customers meet compliance requirements, not a vendor certification held by Fortinet itself.

No explicit policy statement addresses whether Fortinet trains machine learning models on customer data or offers an opt-out. Fortinet's privacy policy mentions using data 'to improve services and develop new features' but does not specify ML training.
The acquisition was completed in August 2024, fewer than two years ago. Product certifications following integration with Fortinet may be in transition.
